context_vs_known_results.summary: The claim sits strictly inside the open gap. Positive side before this paper: Carleson 1966 (L2), Hunt 1968 (Lp, p>1), Sjolin 1969 (L log L log log L), Antonov 1996 (L log L log log log L), Arias de Reyna 2002 (QA), Carro-Mastylo-Rodriguez-Piazza 2012, Lie 2013 (time-frequency proof of QA -> weak L1), Di Plinio-Fragkos 2025. Negative side: Kolmogorov 1923 (L1), Konyagin 2000 (phi(L) with phi(u) = o(u sqrt(log u / log log u)) has everywhere-divergent Fourier series). L log L (phi(u) = u log u) is not excluded by Konyagin, since u log u is not o(u sqrt(log u/log log u)). The claim is therefore consistent with all known results and exactly resolves Lie's Conjecture 1 (JEMS 2017, 'L log L is a C-space', a weak-L1 bound for the full Carleson operator), which the paper's Corollary (via Stein 1961) matches, Orlicz vs Lorentz L log L norms being equivalent on a finite measure space.
context_vs_known_results.lie2017_check: Verified from arXiv 1408.4783 v2: Definition 1 (C-space: ||Cf||_{1,inf} <= C0 ||f||_Y) and 'Conjecture 1. The Lorentz space Y = L log L is a C-space.' The paper cites it as [Lie2017, Definition 1.1 and Conjecture 1]; the published numbering may differ (arXiv: 'Definition 1').
omissions: Konyagin's divergence results (the negative side of the gap) are not cited.
Lie's heuristic that the maximal Lorentz C-space might be L sqrt(log L) (so L log L would not be sharp) is not discussed.
No discussion of the Walsh analogue (Walsh-Carleson near L1, Do-Lacey, Di Plinio), where the same proof template would presumably apply.
context_vs_known_results.also_implied: Since L2 is contained in L log L and the proof never invokes Carleson/Hunt or time-frequency analysis, the paper (and the Lean, which imports only Mathlib and not the carleson library) contains an independent proof of Carleson's theorem.

main_statement.latex: \begin{theorem}[Almost-everywhere convergence in $L\log L$] For every complex-valued $f\in L\log L(\mathbb T)$, there is a measurable set $N_f$ of measure zero such that $\lim_{N\to\infty}S_Nf(x)=f(x)$ $(x\in\mathbb T\setminus N_f)$. The limit is along the full sequence $N=0,1,2,\ldots$. \end{theorem}
main_statement.paraphrase: If int |f| log(2+|f|) < infinity on the circle, then the symmetric Fourier partial sums S_N f converge to f almost everywhere, along all N (not a subsequence).
main_statement.hypothesis_class: sections/01-introduction.tex:88-92: L log L = {f : int |f| log(2+|f|) dmu < infinity}, mu = dx/2pi.

key_estimate.paraphrase: For rho >= 0 of mass 1 and height <= e^d, int over {M rho <= (log d)^4} of sup_N |S_N rho| <= C d; it follows from a finite stopped 'modulated delayed Haar' estimate with the same Cd bound uniformly in depth and number of frequencies.

headline_corollaries.paraphrase: Weak-L1 maximal bound sup_lambda lambda mu{S* f > lambda} <= C ||f||_Phi (Luxemburg, Phi(t) = t log(2+t)), via Stein 1961. This is the form of Lie's Conjecture 1.

proof_architecture.claim: Reduction to one height layer: Thm main follows from Thm good-set (int over G_rho of sup_N |S_N rho| <= Cd for mass-one rho <= e^d, |G_rho^c| <= C (log d)^{-4}) by splitting f into doubly exponential layers, Borel-Cantelli on G_j^c and L1 summation of sum m_j d_j < infinity; bounded layers converge by Prop bounded inputs.

Fourier transfer: sup_N |S_N rho| <= rho + 1 + sup_n |H(rho chi_n)|; truncated H_delta ~ (1/(pi c)) K_J up to bounded error and an inner window <= C M rho; K_J is the translation-and-scale average of the delayed Haar shift (kappa, c = -1/8). So Thm good-set follows from the finite dyadic estimate. (Lean replaces the Hilbert transform by a direct Dirichlet-kernel comparison.)

Entropy compression (Secs 3-4): from a uniform bound on noisy 2T-fold sums of frequencies, extract a large subset S' and a centre x0 whose phase defects are small on one common omega-region, valid for every weight on S'. Proof: Gibbs-dual noisy-sum law -> pinning to nearly iid blocks -> thinning to exact iid -> two-order refinement search raising block length at O(h^{-2}) entropy cost -> freeze and extract phase region.

Thermal labels and spectral update (Sec 5): the input point carries a noisy label with XY-Gibbs noise e^{-A}. If many label-weighted high frequencies are separated, compression yields either a regular test (success probability >= beta/2, later paid by likelihood evidence e^{-t/8}) or a cheap deterministic update that lowers the gap potential F(A) - log|B_A(r)| by k_b/2.

Finite procedure and global budgets (Sec 6): split the input on the dyadic tree into live/static plateaus by spectral tests; per-branch k_b + t <= Cd, n <= Ch; membership surprisal O(h) in L2; plateau weights sum to O(h); transfer probability O(h^{-10}); global label Fisher sum O(d).

Capture and snapshots (Sec 7): cumulative signed-span frequency lists via Riesz-product entropy increments; edge charges via likelihood windows; snapshots of representatives refreshed by a generalized-relative-entropy trigger; one miss block before activation.

Path estimates (Sec 8): predictable-sign maximal inequality; scalar Bellman-type potential for small amplitudes; vector (label-valued) delayed estimate with an absolute coefficient on the Fisher sum; checkpoints and simultaneous parameters over all representatives and dyadic caps.

Assembly (Sec 9): per live plateau the frequency-independent majorant has expectation O(d/h) (main levels decoded via c_A(n) >= 1/2) plus globally charged Fisher/edge terms; times total live weight O(h) gives O(d); static families and rare transfers add O(d). This proves Prop dyadic.

eureka_candidates_ranked.item: I26 + I27 + I10 (cluster): thermal noisy labels of the input point, read through the two-law (true input vs uniform output) Fisher-sum identity
eureka_candidates_ranked.for: This is the device that converts frequency selection into information-theoretic currency: a new random variable Z = Y + theta, never present in the goal or in L, whose Fisher information along output paths is globally bounded by O(d) via the entropy chain rule, while decoding int chi_n a^s = c_A(n) c^{s+n} recovers each modulation. It is the literal analogue of an extension variable: tiny to state, absent from the problem, and it makes the 'separate costs for information and for choosing frequencies' accounting possible. A quick literature check found no information-theoretic or noisy-observation proof of Carleson-type bounds; all known proofs (Carleson, Fefferman, Lacey-Thiele, Lie, Di Plinio) are combinatorial time-frequency arguments.
eureka_candidates_ranked.against: Adding Gaussian-type noise to a random variable and tracking Fisher information is standard in information theory (de Bruijn identity, stochastic localization, entropy-increment proofs). A judge may grade this as cross-field transfer (N2) rather than a new idea. Its payoff also depends on the rest of the cluster (chain depth > 1).

correctness_audit.verdict: No gap found at the level of a careful read of all sections, but the claim is extraordinary: it resolves a 60-year question and gives a new proof of Carleson's theorem. The paper is dense, with many 'sufficiently large d' and polylog(h) bookkeeping steps that we could not check line by line. The strongest evidence for correctness is the sorry-free, axiom-free, Mathlib-only Lean formalization, whose comparator statement exactly matches Thm main. We did not build it, so this evidence is conditional on the release's own claim that it compiles and passes the comparator.
checked: Layer summation (11:279-353): rho_j <= e^{d_j}, sum m_j d_j < infinity from int |f| log|f| < infinity plus the entropy term; sum |G_j^c| <= C sum (log d_j)^{-4} < infinity; Borel-Cantelli and L1 summation are correct.
Bounded-input proposition (11:237-275): d_l chosen so rho_l <= e^{d_l}; m_l d_l -> 0; convergence in measure argument is correct.

Fourier transfer (11:42-227): kappa odd and Lipschitz, c = -1/8 (tent primitive; Lean kappa_integral agrees), K_J = c/t + O(1) on delta < |t| <= 1, inner window <= C M rho <= C e^{4h} = o(d) on G_rho; Pi_{>=0} = (I + iH + P0)/2 and the S_N identity are correct.

Consistency with known lower bounds: Konyagin's divergence threshold phi(u) = o(u sqrt(log u / log log u)) does not reach L log L, so no contradiction; a single layer rho = 1_E/|E| gives S* ~ log(1/|E|) = d on a large set, consistent with the Cd bound.
Stein corollary (11:357-392): hypotheses of Stein's theorem (Banach space, translation-commuting bounded S_N, a.e.-finite maximal function) hold.
Section 3 spot checks: dual formula and weak duality (03:124-188); monotone deficits s_j and the telescoping prefix average (03:320-377); thinning acceptance error delta <= 3 epsilon (03:708-726).
Section 4 spot check: search cost bounds 4 alpha_1 = O(h^{-2}) with N, n ~ exp(h).
residual_concerns: Extraordinary claim, unreviewed, author 'OpenAI'. Expert review and an independent Lean build are needed.

The paper's Prop regular evidence (05:645-771) asserts a simultaneous true-law statement over all regular successes; the Lean Thermal layer proves only per-attempt bounds. Where the simultaneous version (or a substitute) lives is reported under lean_procedure_notes.

Paper and Lean use different parameters: cutoff (log d)^4 vs (j+1)^3 ~ (log d)^3; h = log log d vs ~ log j/1000; L = d e^{(log d)^{1/4}} vs d 2^{2^h}; k_b quadratic vs linear in log(1/b); search schedule M^{1/10}, M^{1/2} vs 2^{16h}. So the Lean certifies the theorem, not every intermediate statement of the paper as written.

Lean replaces the paper's Hilbert-transform route by a direct Dirichlet-kernel comparison and the Fejer/d_j layer bookkeeping by padded masses; the paper's own text for these steps is therefore not what is formalized (both routes look correct).

Konyagin's results (the negative side) are not cited; the paper also does not discuss why the method fails below L log L (e.g. at L sqrt(log L), which Lie suggests may be the true threshold). A 'proves too much' test is therefore missing from the paper: which step uses the full log factor? Our reading: the Cd per-layer bound summed against m_j 2^j uses exactly int |f| log|f|, and every budget is O(d), so the method is calibrated to L log L and does not obviously give more.
Prop dyadic allows arbitrary F_{j+1}-measurable multipliers eps_j shared across modulations; the Lean proves only the eps_j = r_{j+1} case needed. The general statement is unverified.
